description:
docs: warn that P100 GPU compute fails with the default image (#1156)

The default Kaggle image now ships a cu128 PyTorch build with no Pascal
(sm_60) kernels, so requesting NvidiaTeslaP100 allocates a GPU and
torch.cuda.is_available() returns True, but the first real CUDA op dies
with cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice. That's a confusing failure to hit
at runtime, so this adds a caveat wherever the accelerator values are
documented and in the --accelerator help text, pointing users at T4/L4
or a Pascal-compatible torch build.

Note the SDK enum comment requested alongside this isn't in kaggle-cli:
kagglesdk is a pip dependency, and its docstrings are generated from
Kaggle.Sdk/kernels/kernels_api_service.proto in kaggleazure. That needs
a separate PR.

Co-authored-by: kaggle-agent 

---

Task:
[messick-20260730151802-b0a2773b](https://agents.dev.kaggle.net/tasks/messick-20260730151802-b0a2773b)

### Prompt

Add a caveat about NvidiaTeslaP100 to the kaggle-cli docs and SDK.

Context: The default Kaggle Docker image now ships a PyTorch build for
CUDA 12.8 (cu128) that no longer includes CUDA kernel images for Pascal
(compute capability sm_60). As a result, requesting `machine_shape:
"NvidiaTeslaP100"` allocates a P100 and `torch.cuda.is_available()`
returns True, but the first real CUDA operation fails with
`cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice`. T4/L4 work fine. This is an
intentional tradeoff (newer PyTorch was needed for Blackwell / RTX Pro
6000 sm_120 GPUs; P100s are being phased out).

Task: Add a clear caveat next to the `NvidiaTeslaP100` value in BOTH of
these places:

1. `docs/kernels_metadata.md` — wherever `machine_shape` accepted values
/ NvidiaTeslaP100 are documented.
2. The SDK enum/type declaration for machine_shape / GPU accelerators
(`kagglesdk/kernels/types/kernels_api_service.py`) — add a comment on
the NvidiaTeslaP100 enum member.

The caveat should note: the default Kaggle image's PyTorch (cu128) does
not include Pascal (sm_60) kernels, so GPU compute on P100 will fail
with the default image; recommend using NvidiaTeslaT4 (or L4), or
installing a Pascal-compatible torch build if a P100 is required.

Keep the wording concise and match the existing doc style. Do not change
any behavior — docs/comments only.

description:
fix(cli): prevent silent partial uploads on upload failure (#1150)

## Summary

When creating a dataset or model version, a failed file upload could be
silently ignored. If `_upload_blob()` returned `None`—either because the
upload failed or because all resume attempts were exhausted—the file was
skipped, the create request still went through, and the CLI reported
success. This could result in a dataset or model version being created
with one or more missing files.

This change makes upload failures abort the operation instead of
creating a partial upload.

## Fix

* Raise a `ValueError` when a file upload fails instead of returning
`None`.
* Prevent dataset/model version creation if any file upload fails.
* Added a separate `EXPIRED` upload state for resumable uploads whose
session can no longer be resumed.
* Restart the upload only when the session can no longer be resumed (for
example, an expired upload session). A `FAILED` result still gives up,
since the server rejected the upload and restarting would only hit the
same error.
* Updated the upload status documentation to match the implemented
behavior.

## Behavior change

Since `_upload_file()` is shared, this also affects two other commands:

* `kaggle competitions data update` now aborts if any file upload fails
instead of creating a partial data version.
* `kaggle files upload` now aborts if a file upload fails instead of
skipping the failed file and continuing.

The CLI now exits with a non-zero status when an upload fails, making
these failures visible to automation.

## Tests

Added regression tests to verify that:

* Dataset creation aborts when any file upload fails.
* Model version creation aborts when any file upload fails.
* Failed uploads are no longer silently skipped.
* Expired upload sessions start a new upload instead of reusing the old
session.
* Existing successful upload behavior continues to work.

Ran:

* `pytest tests/unit/test_upload_helpers.py`
* `pytest tests/unit/test_dataset_create.py`
* `pytest tests/unit/test_model_create.py`

Also ran the full unit test suite to verify there were no regressions.

This beta adds PRs #831 and #835 on top of v1.0.56-beta.1. It separates
Agent Product observability and IM display identity from the stable
edition-owned PAT and routing identity, and reduces common-path Skill context
loading without changing the public command or Runtime Schema surface.

Changed

  • Agent Product identity separation (#831) — sends DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT through the new x-dws-agent-product observability Header and uses a valid non-empty value for the IM clawType display label whenever --ai-tag is enabled. Because --ai-tag defaults to true, callers that set DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT change the displayed label by default. With --ai-tag=false, native chat message send / reply calls preserve their existing wire shape by sending an empty IM clawType, while shortcut calls omit the argument. Unset or empty Product values omit the Header and preserve the active edition's IM display default.
  • Agent Host dimension convention (#831) — new integrations should send the runtime form (cloud or desktop) through DWS_AGENT_HOST and report the product separately through DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT. Legacy combined labels such as qwenwork_cloud remain syntactically valid for compatibility.
  • Reduced common-path Skill context (#835) — keeps the complete 97-command Chat Shortcut inventory in Runtime Catalog and leaf Schema while routing common intents through compact Skill tables and references. When an exact command path is already known, the mono Skill no longer requires eager loading of a complete product reference. The generated Skill policy now detects drift, forced full-reference loading, and context-budget regressions; the common Chat plus shared activation estimate drops from 7,301 to 4,771 o200k_base tokens without changing the 845-tool Schema surface.

Fixed

  • Stable PAT/routing identity (#831) — restores the CLI-emitted open-source HTTP claw-type and PAT hostControl.clawType to the edition-fixed openClaw value. DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT no longer changes those wire values, and the client continues to derive PAT, authentication, routing, and Discovery behaviour from the existing independent signals.
  • Portable generated Skill validation (#835) — resolves the mono Skill name by scanning upward from the generated target, keeping --check independent of the repository checkout path and preventing false drift failures when an ancestor directory resembles a Skill name.

This beta supersedes the unpublished v1.0.55-beta.6 candidate and packages
PRs #621, #676, #757, #815, #816, and #821. It restores the mandatory
multi-account safety rule caught by the sealed-release E2E gate while retaining
the reviewed Wukong capability and multi-Skill synchronization, declarative
command and Schema delivery, hardened Chat shortcuts, external contact
resolution, and Agent product identity on top of the v1.0.55-beta.5 baseline.

Added

  • Wukong capability and multi-Skill synchronization (#621) — ports roughly 30 reviewed leaf commands into the open-source CLI across Drive, Doc, Sheet, and Chat, including in-place text-emotion updates, Drive version and permission operations, document styling, and Sheet comment/version/formula verification. The bundled multi-Skill framework is reorganized into progressive product references and routing guidance while retaining current open-source command, response, safety, and Runtime Schema contracts.
  • Declarative leaf commands and unified metadata delivery (#676) — adds the reusable LeafSpec command framework and migrates 27 DevApp commands without changing their paths or flags. Runtime consumers now resolve identity, safety, and selection through one embedded Catalog-backed API, and guarded Help output publishes the command's safety/confirmation annotation.
  • Agent product identity (#816) — adds the optional DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT override for the existing HTTP claw-type header while preserving each edition's default when unset. Product and runtime labels are caller-declared signals, not authentication credentials; services must validate supported values and must not grant access solely from them. The override does not change the separate IM message-display clawType parameter controlled by the edition and --ai-tag.

Changed

  • Reviewed Chat shortcut delivery (#815) — publishes 88 currently available Chat shortcuts after real-business validation, keeps three confirmed lower-service failures unavailable, strengthens semantic availability and dry-run contracts, and adds safe message-resource download plus group-member listing. Conversation filtering, IM routing/reporting, and member mute resolution are aligned with the validated backend identities.
  • Agent identity label hardening (#816) — limits DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT and DWS_AGENT_HOST to 64 ASCII bytes, trims only surrounding ASCII spaces and tabs, and rejects other control or Unicode whitespace. QwenWork integrations should report the two dimensions separately as DWS_AGENT_PRODUCT=qwenwork plus DWS_AGENT_HOST=cloud or desktop; previously used combined Host labels such as qwenwork_cloud remain syntactically valid for compatibility.

Fixed

  • External-contact and message-resource chaining (#757) — the shared name-to-ID resolver keeps external or cross-organization contacts that expose only openDingTalkId, applies reviewed display-name fallbacks, and preserves organization-only filtering for commands that require userId. chat +messages-resource-url now accepts --msg-id and --open-message-id as aliases for --message-id, matching message-list response fields.
  • Multi-account Skill safety contract (#821) — restores the mandatory rule that an Agent must never choose the first, most recently logged-in, or most recently used account when an organization has multiple accounts without one unique isOrgCurrent=true default. A PR-level embedded-Skill regression test now catches removal before the full sealed-release E2E gate.

description:
fix(docx): style decomposition falls back to raw-set for any SDK-unrebuildable child

Bug: dump --format batch on a document whose styles carry a child that is only
valid outside a style context replayed as "Unknown element type 'w:X'". Known
instances: `w:tcBorders` in a table style's , and `w:rtl` in a paragraph
style's  (RTL/CJK styles).

Root cause: recursive style/numbering decomposition emitted a typed `add w:X`
for every element that passed the static residue checks (known namespace, no
text, no external relationship). But the generic add can only rebuild an element
the SDK schema accepts under the reconstructed parent — and a style-context
container is a different SDK type than its body counterpart (a style  is
StyleRunProperties, a style  is StyleTableCellProperties), rejecting
children the flat-XML tree carries. The prior fix hardcoded the one discovered
offender (w:tcBorders), so the next such child (w:rtl) broke replay again.

Fix: replace the per-element denylist with the SDK's own type table. Parse the
part through the SDK alongside the flat XML and walk the two trees in lockstep;
an element the SDK resolves to OpenXmlUnknownElement in its typed parent context
is exactly what the generic add's TryCreateTypedElement returns null for, so
treat it as residue — the recursion unwinds and the whole  / part ships
verbatim via raw-set (the existing safety net). A parse failure or any tree
desync (length or localName mismatch at a slot) also falls back to raw-set.

New behavior: any style/numbering child unbuildable in its context (tcBorders,
rtl, and future RTL/CJK style children) round-trips via raw-set without a new
per-element special case; children the generic add can rebuild still decompose,
so raw-set coverage does not widen beyond the genuinely-unreconstructable set.

description:
docs(batch): document the clean-slate dump->batch replay idiom

Replaying a dump into a target that may already exist — and may be held by a
live resident — is a recurring foot-gun for scripted consumers. `create`
refuses to overwrite an existing file (file_exists) and refuses one a resident
still pins (file_locked), both exit 1; a script that ignores create's exit code
then replays onto the previous run's document, so add-style / add-bookmark
items fail with "already exists".

Add a short note to the batch command help spelling out the reliable idiom
(close -> rm -> create -> batch -> close), why rm must precede create (a gone
on-disk file lets create auto-close a resident pinning that path; the leading
close only covers the handle-release window), and that `create --force`
overwrites but does not release a resident lock.

dropping a vbaProject, not an omission.

byte content and macroEnabled content-type survive, validate passes, and

Added

  • New meeting search subcommand (cmd/meeting/search.go, internal/cmdutil/api_schema.go): Keyword / meeting-code / time-window search for meetings, complementing the pure time-window meeting list and meeting list-ended. Backed by the new GET /v1/meetings/search-meetings endpoint and wired through the standard middleware chain (WithApiCmd(ApiCmdMeetingSearch) + WithCompact). All filter flags are optional and freely combinable.
    • --query — Search keyword; bounded by maxQueryLen = 50 runes and validated via utils.CharacterLimit.
    • --query-field (default all) — Field to match --query against: subject / creator (creator nickname or remark name) / note (user's private note on the meeting) / all.
    • --meeting-code — Exact-match meeting code; normalized via the new cmdutil.FormatMeetingCode before being sent to the server.
    • --start / --end — ISO 8601 window bounds. The server matches a meeting if any of its scheduled start, actual start, or the current user's join time falls inside the window. --start >= --end is rejected client-side with InvalidArgsError.
    • --page-token / --page-size (default 30, max 30, capped via cmdutil.ClampingPageSize + cmdutil.PageSizeMaxMeetings) — Standard v1.0.5 pagination.
    • Response is post-processed with MeetingTypeConverter + the new MeetingStatusInSearchConverter at meetings.status, then WithCompact and WithTotalCountLogic (see below).
  • New record search subcommand (cmd/record/search.go, internal/cmdutil/api_schema.go): Keyword / meeting-code / meeting-id / time-window / file-type search across recordings and their AI-derived artifacts (transcript / smart minutes / timeline). Backed by GET /v1/mcp/records/search and wired through WithApiCmd(ApiCmdRecordSearch) + WithCompact.
    • --query (bounded by maxQueryLen = 50 runes, validated via utils.CharacterLimit) and --query-field (default all) — Field set is subject / creator / transcript_content / smart_minutes / timeline / all; the last three let the user grep the recording's derived content, not just its metadata.
    • --file-type (default all) — Restrict results to video / audio / transcript / upload / external / all.
    • --meeting-id / --meeting-code — Optional filters; --meeting-code is normalized via cmdutil.FormatMeetingCode.
    • --start / --end — ISO 8601 window bounds with the same start >= end client-side guard.
    • --page-token / --page-size (default 30, max 30, capped via cmdutil.PageSizeMaxRecords).
  • New MeetingStatusInSearch string enum and converter (internal/utils/enumerate/meeting_status_in_search.go, internal/utils/enumerate/meeting_status_in_search_test.go, internal/utils/converter.go): Maps the search endpoint's status values unknown / upcoming / in_progress / closed to their Chinese display names (未知状态 / 待开始 / 进行中 / 已结束). Unrecognized inputs fall back to Unknown. Wired into meeting search output at path meetings.status via the new MeetingStatusInSearchConverter (stringEnumConverter-backed).
  • New output.WithTotalCountLogic output option (internal/output/options.go): When the response's top-level total_count is 0, the field is stripped from the payload via utils.DeleteFields (maxDepth=10) so the caller does not see a misleading zero (typically emitted by the server as a placeholder before the real count is computed). Wired into meeting search, record search, and record list. Non-zero counts are preserved as-is.
  • New cmdutil.FormatMeetingCode normalization helper and companion unit tests (internal/cmdutil/meeting_help.go, internal/cmdutil/meeting_help_test.go): Accepts the four common ways users copy a meeting code — #腾讯会议：295-150-176, 295-150-176, 295 150 176, 295150176 — and reduces every form to the bare digit string. Strips the #腾讯会议： / #腾讯会议: prefix (full-width and half-width colon), then removes hyphens, spaces, tabs, and single quotes via a single strings.NewReplacer. Applied at every entry point that accepts a meeting code: meeting get, meeting search, record list, record search. Replaces the ad-hoc single-quote stripping added in v1.0.13.
  • JSON output stops HTML-escaping < / > / & (internal/output/print.go): New internal marshalNoEscape helper wraps json.Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) and strips the trailing newline that Encoder.Encode appends, so the top-level FormatPrint output preserves URLs, query strings, and other verbatim text exactly as the server returned them. Both json and json-pretty formats use the new helper.
  • New output.MetaKeyFilterField exported constant (internal/output/options.go): The v1.0.12 metaKeyFilterField sentinel is now exported so downstream callers (and the SKILL / docs) can reference the reserved filter_field meta key by name instead of hard-coding the string.

Changed

description:
fix(draft): refuse body edits on reply drafts instead of splicing the quoted-history boundary (closes #159) (#160)

* spec(email-write,provider-microsoft): propose update-draft-body-safety

Retire the quoted-history boundary heuristic in update_draft. Reply drafts
refuse body edits with a recoverable error; non-reply drafts allow a wholesale
replace behind explicit replace_body. Reply status is determined from Graph
metadata and fails closed. Subject renames on replies stay permitted and emit a
non-blocking threading warning rather than being refused.

Validated with `openspec validate update-draft-body-safety --strict`.

Refs #159.

* fix(draft): refuse body edits on reply drafts instead of splicing the quoted-history boundary

update_draft decided how to PATCH a body by searching the body HTML for a
quoted-history boundary. Both shipped variants failed silently: splicing at the
first 
 let any authored markdown `---` become a false boundary and stack a
second copy of the message, while an exact `divRplyFwdMsg` match fell through to
a wholesale replace that deleted the entire quoted thread. The marker is not
stable enough to carry that weight — Gmail prefixes it as m_ and nests
on each round trip, Exchange prefixes it as x_, and Outlook mobile uses a
different container element entirely.

Reply status now comes from Graph metadata rather than body content, and fails
closed. Reply drafts refuse body edits with a recoverable
REPLY_DRAFT_BODY_IMMUTABLE error; non-reply drafts replace wholesale behind an
explicit replace_body opt-in. Subject renames on replies stay permitted and
emit a non-blocking threading warning rather than being refused.

Implements openspec/changes/update-draft-body-safety.

Peer review (agy + Codex) pending.

Closes #159.

* fix(draft): make reply detection fail closed and resolve Gmail drafts by draft id

Peer review (agy + Codex) found the previous detection failed OPEN. An empty
internetMessageHeaders array — the plausible shape for an unsent draft, since
those are transport headers Graph does not promise to populate before send —
passed the Array.isArray guard, found no In-Reply-To, and returned 'non_reply'.
A reply draft was then positively declared safe, replace_body was accepted, and
the quoted thread destroyed: the exact defect this branch exists to fix.

Detection no longer reads internetMessageHeaders. Drafts this application
creates carry an authoritative extended-property origin stamp. Drafts created
elsewhere fall back to conversationIndex, decoded and compared by byte length
(root is 22 bytes; Exchange appends 5 per reply or forward), with strict base64
validation so malformed input cannot decode to a spurious length. Everything
else is indeterminate, which refuses the edit. No path now yields 'non_reply'
from absence of evidence.

Gmail resolved a draft-resource id against users.messages.get; draft ids and
message ids are distinct. Added drafts.get and resolve draft.message in the
status, update, and preview read-back paths.

Peer review round 2 pending.

Refs #159.

* fix(draft): only an application-written origin stamp may classify a draft non_reply

Peer review round 2 split: agy approved, Codex did not. Codex sustained.

Conversation-tree position is not the same proposition as absence of quoted
history. A 22-byte conversationIndex proves a draft is a conversation root; it
does not prove the body carries no quotes, because an imported, copied,
migrated or hand-composed draft can be a root and still contain them. Inferring
Gmail freshness from a missing In-Reply-To has the same defect — an externally
created forward can carry provider-assembled quoted history with no such header.

replace_body: true is the caller asserting "replace the body", not "I accept
losing quoted history". Answering non_reply tells the caller the operation is
safe, so that answer must never rest on evidence of a different proposition.

Both providers now return non_reply only from an origin stamp this application
wrote at creation. Graph drops the conversationIndex length fallback (a longer
index may still yield reply, which refuses anyway); Gmail gains an
X-Agent-Draft-Origin header baked into the raw MIME. scheduleMessage stamps the
draft it creates, so a failed send cannot strand an unstamped one. The test
asserting non_reply for a structurally invalid 0x5a x 22 index is removed with
the branch it exercised.

Accepted consequence: body edits are unavailable on drafts this application did
not create. The documented remedy — create a new draft — covers that case.

Peer review round 3 pending.

Refs #159.

* fix(draft): resolve conflicting duplicate origin stamps to indeterminate

Peer review round 3 (Codex) held that the origin stamp proves a value, not
authorship, since any client with draft-write access can set it. Overridden and
recorded as accepted risk in design.md: an actor able to forge the stamp already
holds write access to the draft and can replace its body directly, so routing
the same damage through this tool grants no additional capability. An
authenticated draft-bound stamp would add secret management and rotation to
defend against an adversary who already has the power in question.

The duplicate-header half of that finding is taken. Taking the first match made
the answer depend on header or collection ordering, so a draft carrying two
conflicting stamps resolved arbitrarily. Both providers now require a single
unanimous stamp; conflicting or unrecognised values are indeterminate, which
refuses the edit. Regression tests cover conflicting duplicates, unanimous
duplicates, and an unrecognised value on both providers.

Refs #159.

description:
feat(email-core): add opt-in raw-HTML output to read_email (#157)

* feat(email-core): add opt-in raw-HTML output to read_email

`read_email` always converted the body to markdown, so a formatted body
could not be round-tripped. Take a body carrying hand-applied inline
styling that only exists in HTML — red strikethrough and blue underline
marking proposed edits, a background highlight on a figure under
discussion. An agent needing to change one sentence and leave every other
byte alone had two options: go through markdown and watch htmlToMarkdown
destroy the styling on the way out, or ask a human to copy the formatted
body out of the mail client by hand. The second is what actually happened,
twice in one day across roughly fifteen revisions of a single message.

The write path was already capable — renderEmailBody treats format: 'html'
as a pure passthrough with no write-path sanitiser. The gap was entirely on
the read side: read.ts unconditionally called transformEmailContent, and
ReadEmailOutput had no HTML field at all, so the provider handed us
bodyHtml and the action threw it away before any caller could see it.

Adds format?: 'markdown' | 'html' to the input, defaulting to 'markdown'.
The markdown default is deliberate and stays — it is what keeps a routine
read cheap — so this is strictly additive and opt-in, with a test asserting
the omitted-format body is byte-identical to explicitly passing the
pre-existing defaults.

The 'html' branch returns msg.bodyHtml verbatim: no markdown conversion, no
appended attachment summary, and no strip_quoted_history/strip_signatures.
All three rewrite the string, and byte fidelity is the entire feature —
stripSignature in particular cuts by a length-percentage heuristic that has
no meaning over HTML and would happily amputate a closing tag. Attachments
are still reported structurally, so nothing is lost.

Two output fields come with it. bodyFormat ('markdown' | 'html' | 'text')
is required and always present, following the recipient-topology precedent
from #102: an omitted key is ambiguous, and 'html' requested on a message
with no HTML part yields the plain-text body, which must be distinguishable
from real HTML because writing it back as HTML would mangle it.
bodyTruncated is set only when it fires, mirroring DraftPreviewSchema —
it is a warning, and its absence is what tells a caller the body is safe to
write back.

READ_HTML_BODY_LIMIT is 256 KB rather than the 32 KB PREVIEW_BODY_LIMIT. A
preview exists so an agent can eyeball what was persisted; a raw-HTML read
exists so it can round-trip a body, and a truncated body cannot be written
back at all. Outlook HTML with inline mso- styling routinely runs past
32 KB for a body whose markdown reduction is a few KB, so that cap would
truncate the majority of the bodies this exists to serve. The byte-safe cut
helper itself is now exported from compose-helpers and shared, so the two
truncation signals cannot disagree about a codepoint boundary.

README documents both halves of the round trip: read_email's format, and
the compose-side format that was already implemented but undocumented.

Fixes: #156

* fix(email-core): address peer review on read_email html format

Codex peer review returned FAIL with one blocker and three should-fixes.
All four were right.

Blocker — the byte-preserving round trip was a false claim. renderEmailBody
defaults forceBlack to true even for format: 'html', so writing a body back
wraps it in a force-black div and every cycle nests another one; Codex
reproduced three nested wrappers in three cycles. Fifteen revisions of a
message would carry fifteen. The compose-side default is deliberately NOT
changed: it is correct for its actual job, HTML the agent authored itself,
possibly a bare fragment with no colour of its own that Outlook dark mode
would render white-on-white. Flipping it for format: 'html' would silently
change how every existing HTML sender's mail renders in a published package,
to fix something that only arises on the read-back path. Instead both tool
descriptions and both READMEs now state that writing raw HTML back requires
force_black: false, and a test pins both directions — three cycles with the
flag off are byte-identical, and the wrapper demonstrably appears with it on.

The truncation cap was applied to the plain-text fallback while the docs said
it only applied to raw HTML. Keeping the cap and fixing the wording: the text
fallback is still a format: 'html' response headed for the same transport
budget, and an unbounded one cut by the transport instead would arrive
mangled with no flag on it. The markdown path stays uncapped. Adds a
regression test for an oversized text-only body, asserting the same message
comes back in full and unflagged on the default path.

The default-unchanged test compared the new function against itself with
hand-passed arguments, which drifts in sympathy with the implementation and
proves nothing — and its two calls disagreed about strip_signatures, masked
by a fixture with no signature in it. Replaced with a golden string, the
default resolved through input.parse() rather than passed by hand, over
fixtures that actually fire the html to markdown conversion, the attachment
summary, retained quoted history, and the signature pass.

packages/email-agent-mcp/README.md is the README that ships in the npm
tarball and still described read_email as markdown-only. Documented there
too.

Ref: #156

* docs(email-core): fix truncation wording and translated tool rows

Codex round 2 returned PASS with one should-fix and one nit; both are docs.

The proposal's summary bullet still said bodyTruncated fires only for a
raw-HTML body, contradicting the implemented plain-text-fallback cap and the
proposal's own later paragraph. Restated to cover both bodies the html branch
can return, and to say the markdown path stays uncapped.

The four translated package READMEs ship in the npm tarball and still
described read_email as markdown-only. The repo has not kept their prose in
sync since #32, so the body-format section is not duplicated into them, but
the tool-reference row is a one-line factual claim and is now correct in all
four.

description:
Serve UI extension source maps during app dev

The built bundle ends with a relative `//# sourceMappingURL=.js.map`, so
the browser requests the map next to the asset's own URL —
`/assets//.js.map` — a key no asset payload emits. The request
404'd and DevTools only ever showed minified output.

Register that key on the asset resolver when the map exists, and serve `.js.map`
requests from the extension directory. Maps are deliberately absent from the
bundle: `keepBuiltSourcemapsLocally` moves them back into the extension
directory so `.js.map` files never reach a deploy bundle. No build step changes,
so that invariant is untouched.

Unregistered `.js.map` paths 404, keeping the resolver the allowlist for this
route.
